headline: Supreme Court Overturns Conviction Of Former South Korean PM Han
seoTitle: Supreme Court Overturns Former South Korean PM Han…
metaDescription: South Korea's top court has overturned the 15-year prison sentence for former Prime Minister Han Duck-so regarding his role in a 2024 martial law case.
aiSummaryBullets: The Supreme Court of South Korea overturned a 15-year prison sentence previously handed to former Prime Minister Han Duck-so.
The legal proceedings involve the former official's alleged role in providing legitimacy to the 2024 martial law declaration.
The case has been sent back to a lower court for further review following the Supreme Court's ruling.
aiContextParagraph: The Supreme Court of South Korea issued a significant legal decision on November 19, 2026, regarding the 2024 martial law declaration. The court vacated the 15-year prison sentence of former Prime Minister Han Duck-so, who had been convicted for his involvement in supporting the martial law decree. This ruling mandates that the case return to a lower court for new deliberations. Separately, the Supreme Court also finalized a four-year prison sentence for a former first lady concerning unrelated corruption charges. These judicial developments represent a notable series of rulings from the nation's highest court, addressing both insurrection-related allegations and corruption claims involving senior officials. The legal status of these high-profile figures remains a focal point of the ongoing judicial review process within the country's legislative and political framework.
whyItIsViral: The story gained traction due to high-velocity reporting across multiple news outlets covering the final judicial rulings on high-profile government figures.
